audit: FULL AUDIT 2026-05-29 — Security Deep + RBAC + Sanctum + Spatie
head: 5032dc158
scope: RBAC + Sanctum kiosk:order + BlockKioskMiddleware + channels.php + Loyalty HMAC + FormRequest authz drift + IDOR + mass-assignment + XSS/v-html
methodology: Static analysis only (no live HTTP). All file:line citations grep-confirmed against HEAD 5032dc158. Reproductions described as PHP unit-test-style or curl-equivalent.
context_v1_local: V1 Le Cayenne single-branch single-machine (branch_id=1). Multi-branch P0s downgraded to P1 in V1 LOCAL scope but remain P0 for V2 SaaS cutover.

findings.title: Cross-branch staff escalation via mass-assignment of branch_id on /api/admin/{waiter,chef,delivery-boy,employee} CRUD
findings.attack: Branch Manager (or any role granted *_create / *_edit) attaches arbitrary branch_id in JSON body. Service does $request->branch_id verbatim into User::create / $user->save without comparing against Auth::user()->branch_id. Result: a manager of branch=3 can create / migrate a Waiter / Chef / Employee / DeliveryBoy onto branch=5, where that user then logs in, falls under BranchScope for branch=5, and reads / mutates branch=5 orders, cash sessions, KDS queue.
repro: 1. Auth as Branch Manager bound to branch=3 (Sanctum or session).

2. POST /api/admin/waiter with body {name:'Mallory', email:'m@evil.com', phone:'+33000000001', password:'Aaaaaaaaaa1!', password_confirmation:'Aaaaaaaaaa1!', branch_id:5, status:1, country_code:'FR'}.
4. WaiterRequest::authorize returns true; rule for branch_id is only [nullable, numeric] — no caller-branch validation.
5. WaiterService::store at line 72 executes User::create([..., 'branch_id' => $request->branch_id, ...]) → user persists with branch_id=5.
6. Mallory logs in, BranchScope scopes all queries to branch=5 → cross-branch escalation.
findings.evidence: grep -n branch_id app/Services/WaiterService.php → lines 72 ('branch_id' => $request->branch_id) and 110 ($this->waiter->branch_id = $request->branch_id) confirm verbatim assignment. No call to Auth::user()->branch_id or assertSameBranch helper anywhere in WaiterService / ChefService / EmployeeService / DeliveryBoyService.
findings.v1_local_impact: ZERO active impact — V1 Le Cayenne is single-branch (branch_id=1). No 'other branches' exist for V1. Branch=0 (admin) is never the target of these endpoints (they assignRole CUSTOMER/WAITER/CHEF etc., never ADMIN — confirmed via $blockRoles guard).
findings.v2_saas_impact: P0 — direct cross-branch RBAC escalation when V2 onboards >1 branch. Becomes a tenant-isolation breach the moment a second branch exists.
findings.fix_suggestion: In each *Service::store|update, before User::create / save: if (Auth::user()->branch_id !== 0 && (int)$request->branch_id !== (int)Auth::user()->branch_id) abort(403, 'Cross-branch staff assignment denied'). Admin (branch_id=0) remains unconstrained. Mirror PosLoyaltyController:53-56 pattern.

findings.title: FormRequest authorize() return-true drift — actual count 75 vs CLAUDE.md baseline 66 (sentinel ceiling 69)
findings.attack: Not a single-exploit per se — each `return true;` defers authorization to whatever (if any) Spatie middleware sits on the route. If a NEW FormRequest with `return true;` is wired to a route WITHOUT `permission:*`, the call is wide-open. The drift from baseline 66 → 75 (delta +9) indicates 9 new authorize-true FormRequests added since 2026-05-21 and the sentinel constant 69 was not raised, but more importantly the count exceeds the sentinel — the sentinel would FAIL on this branch.
findings.repro: grep -rE 'return true;' app/Http/Requests/ | wc -l → returns 75. CLAUDE.md §9 baseline=66, sentinel constant=69. count > ceiling → sentinel fails (count<=baseline rule from CLAUDE.md §9).
findings.evidence: 75 files listed by grep -rln 'return true;' app/Http/Requests/. None of the 9 new files were inspected for route binding — many may be permission-gated at controller level (defense in depth).
findings.v1_local_impact: LOW — V1 LOCAL has single admin; sensitive routes are double-gated by Spatie permission:* at controller level. But sentinel test is RED on this branch, blocking CI / GO-CONDITIONAL.
findings.v2_saas_impact: P1 — drift accumulation surface grows; one new endpoint without a route-level permission middleware becomes an open door.
findings.fix_suggestion: Option A (preferred): identify the 9 new files, refactor each authorize() to `return (bool) $this->user()?->can('<perm>')` if route lacks permission middleware. Option B (interim): lower sentinel RETURN_TRUE_BASELINE constant from 69 to actual 75 after audit confirms each new file is route-gated. Option B is technical-debt accrual.

findings.title: ABSENCE of `abilities:kiosk:order` route-level middleware on /api/frontend/order/* group — design choice but worth surfacing
findings.line: 1269 (route group declaration with comment explaining the omission)
findings.attack: If FormRequest authorize() ever drifts to `return true;` on OrderRequest / OrderStatusRequest / PaymentConfirmRequest / PromoValidateRequest / PricingPreviewRequest, ability scoping is lost. Currently OrderRequest:46-83, OrderStatusRequest:93, PaymentConfirmRequest:20, PromoValidateRequest:19, PricingPreviewRequest:30 all check tokenCan('kiosk:order') — defense holds, but it is a FORM-REQUEST-ONLY layer. The route comment at api.php:1263-1267 explains the choice (session auth has no token, abilities middleware throws 401). Acceptable tradeoff but worth a sentinel.
findings.evidence: grep -B1 -A15 'ability:kiosk:order' routes/api.php returns the comment at lines 1263-1267 acknowledging the design.
findings.v1_local_impact: ZERO. All five FormRequests confirmed to enforce tokenCan today.
findings.status: VALIDATED — defense in depth via FormRequest layer is intact. Recommend a sentinel test that the five FormRequests retain their tokenCan('kiosk:order') discriminator.
findings.fix_suggestion: Add sentinel: tests/Feature/Security/KioskOrderAbilitySentinelTest that asserts OrderRequest::authorize / OrderStatusRequest::authorize / PaymentConfirmRequest::authorize / PromoValidateRequest::authorize / PricingPreviewRequest::authorize all explicitly call tokenCan('kiosk:order').

findings.title: User.php $fillable exposes branch_id + status + email_verified_at — relies on caller discipline at service layer
findings.attack: If any new controller/service ever does User::create($request->all()) or $user->fill($request->validated()) on a route bound to a permissive FormRequest, branch_id / status / email_verified_at become user-settable. Today every observed call site (SignupController:86, GuestSignupController:116, CustomerService:65, WaiterService:66, ChefService, EmployeeService, DeliveryBoyService) uses an EXPLICIT field list — no ::create($request->all()) found. Discipline is intact, but the fillable surface is broad.
findings.repro: Static. No actual exploit path today.
findings.evidence: grep -rn '->fill(\$request' app/ → zero hits. grep -rn 'User::create' → six hits, all with explicit hand-built arrays.
findings.status: VALIDATED — informational. Recommend a sentinel grep-test that no ::create(\$request->all()) or fill(\$request->validated()) targeting User exists.
findings.fix_suggestion: Optional — narrow User $fillable to exclude branch_id + email_verified_at + status; force services to set those via explicit property assignment. Cost: minor — must audit every User::create call. Benefit: defense in depth against future drift.

findings.title: BlockKioskTokenFromAdminRoutes middleware is wired on both /api/admin/* groups
findings.evidence: grep 'block_kiosk_token_admin' routes/api.php returns 4 hits including 2 actual route group middleware arrays at lines 273 and 294. Middleware alias defined at app/Http/Kernel.php:146.
findings.status: VALIDATED — Layer 1 of J-ADV-6 PATH-1 fix is live, not dead code.

findings.title: channels.php branch.{branchId} uses token NAME discriminator immune to Sanctum '*' wildcard
findings.evidence: Lines 44-50 read $user->currentAccessToken()?->name and compare to literal 'kiosk-token'. Wildcard tokens never match because they are named 'auth_token' (LoginController:113 pattern). Admin/Tenant Admin branch fan-out gated by hasRole at line 56 (not bare branch_id===0) closing the guest-Echo-bypass.
findings.status: VALIDATED — R3 T-3.2.2 Sec F-SEC-W6-01/02 fixes intact.

findings.title: LOYALTY_QR_SECRET strength enforced at boot (production guard)
findings.evidence: Boot guard at AppServiceProvider.php:241 reads config('loyalty.qr.secret') and throws RuntimeException if empty in production. LoyaltyQrSigner.php:221-241 enforces min 32-char length AND rejects dev sentinels (changeme, test, dev, secret, dev-loyalty-qr-secret-do-not-use-in-prod). LoyaltyController.php:736 has a defense-in-depth fallback to app.key if config is unset (only reached if boot guard somehow allowed empty — defensive).

findings.title: PosLoyaltyController + PosOrderController post-fetch branch check on withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope)
supporting_files: app/Http/Controllers/Admin/PosOrderController.php:150-158 (mirror pattern with 403 on cross-branch and on ModelNotFoundException — timing-leak fix)
findings.evidence: Both controllers use Order::withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class) for the cross-branch-aware lookup then immediately check $userBranchId !== 0 && !== $order->branch_id → 403. PosOrderController:151 also catches ModelNotFoundException and rewraps as 403 to prevent existence enumeration.
findings.status: VALIDATED — HEAL-A.1 + RED-team Wave 5I A.1 fixes intact.

findings.title: v-html sinks in Vue components all use safeHtml() / DOMPurify
findings.evidence: All four v-html bindings prefix the expression with safeHtml(...) helper. eslint-disable comments at each site reference 'sanitized via DOMPurify'. Vue's {{ }} auto-escape protects the rest of the templates.
findings.status: VALIDATED — no raw user-data sink in v-html.
